# BOOK 1 — Cole of Spyglass Mountain (Arthur Preston Hankins, 1923)

## Front matter
Title page: COLE OF SPYGLASS MOUNTAIN, by Arthur Preston Hankins, author of "The Jubilee Girl" and "The Heritage of the Hills." Dodd, Mead and Company, 1923. Dedicated to Maynard Shipley (scientific material). Chapter list: I The Slug; II Spawn of the Devil; III The Girl at the Crescent; IV The Gypo Queen; V The Gypo Camp; VI The Wreck of the Good Ship "Argo"; VII Joshua Walks with His Father; VIII Number 5635; IX Truth and Honor; X Pardoned; XI An Offer of Partnership; XII Whimpermeter; XIII The Partnership Dissolved; XIV Man and the Slug; XV Out West; XVI The Road to G-String; XVII Ambitions; XVIII New Prospects; XIX A Trio of Shocks; XX "A Little Sleep"; XXI The Surrender; XXII Hercules and His Firebrand; XXIII "When the Moment Comes!"; XXIV Water at Ragtown; XXV On the Rocky Road to Ragtown; XXVI The Moron; XXVII "Nuttin' but de Trut'"; XXVIII "You'll Come Back to Spyglass Mountain"; XXIX Winter in the San Antones; XXX Slim Wolfgang Plans; XXXI Bullets from Spyglass Mountain; XXXII The Night of June Fifteenth; XXXIII Horsemen in the Night; XXXIV When the Moment Came.

## Ch I – The Slug
Spring, weedy swampy city lot. Four boys aged 11–15. Master of ceremonies: Joshua "Cole" Cole (black hair, gray-blue eyes, ascetic Grecian nose, nearly 14). Imprisons slug (Limax campestris) on a chip 4 inches off ground; bet over whether it can get down without jumping/falling. Bets: Towhead's milky/moony agate; Cole's black-and-white striped agate. Towhead runs to school. Brother Lester Cole (11) stays. Slug lowers itself on a mucus thread. Cole lets it down, drops chip ("wouldn't be fair"), Lester loses. Teacher Silvanus Madmallet ("Ole Madhouse," "Ole Sorehammer," "Ole Hothatchet") tardies the brothers. Madmallet punishes Lester first; Joshua refuses to sit, threatens; Madmallet fetches leather strap; Joshua grabs iron poker from the stove coal-box, goes into hall.

## Ch II – Spawn of the Devil
Background: Madmallet thinks Joshua devil's spawn; Joshua bad at arithmetic/grammar, good at composition; read Proctor's *Other Worlds Than Ours* (sent home). Father drowned Joshua in tub. In the hall, Joshua threatens with poker; Madmallet backs down; Madmallet expels Joshua and suspends Lester a week; letter to father. Joshua hides in vacant lot; plans to go West. Plans to intercept messenger Slinky Dawson (teacher's pet) with note; goes home for father's razor (via Zida Hunt, negro cook; lies he forgot a book). Razor-walking slug experiment; Joshua explains slug's undersurface "foot."

## Ch III – The Girl at the Crescent
Father John Cole: traveling hardware salesman, drinker, womanizer, gambler (fast horses); mother Blanche Florence (old Maryland family, came with Lord Calvert) cut off. Father half-drowns Joshua for heresy books (Steele's Chemistry, Darwin, Huxley). Joshua and Lester plan to intercept Slinky Dawson at vacant lot; Joshua threatens him; takes note addressed "Mrs. John H. Cole, Three fifty-five Grant Avenue. Kindness of Albert Dawson"; tears it up. Crescent Skating Rink: Joshua skates, taught opera troupe lady; meets girl with reddish-golden hair and reddish-brown eyes, asks to teach her skating.

## Ch IV – The Gypo Queen
Girl: Madge Mundy, 11, daughter of Bloodmop Mundy (red hair, railroad contractor "gypo man"); mother Black-haired, teaches Madge. Joshua 14 (nearly 15). Madge explains gypo/shanty camp, gypo queen; offers to ask father for work for Joshua and Lester. Joshua reveals expulsion. Lester gone home. Spud Mulligan sent to Cole house; told Lester is locked up.

## Ch V – The Gypo Camp
Joshua spends night in empty boxcar, five cents left; sleeps; switchman directs to camp. Madge invites him to breakfast; mother Elizabeth Mundy ("'Lizabeth") refined; Bloodmop (blue eyes, crow's-feet, "Well, I'm a son-of-a-gun") offers work (driving mules "Jack and Ned," sticking pigs). Mother asks about his life.

## Ch VI – The Wreck of the Good Ship "Argo"
Bloodmop talks with wife about Joshua; Ambrose (old Cole stable man) confirms father's cruelty; cops hunting Joshua. Mrs. Mundy suspects Madge's attachment; Bloodmop jokes about marrying Madge to Joshua (Florence family wealth). Joshua and Madge under starlit sky: Orion, Betelgeuse, Rigel, Sirius, Pointer to Pole Star; "Ship Argo" quote. Detective Dickinson arrives: Joshua has father's razor; captured by Lester's report/father's telegram.

## Ch VII – Joshua Walks with His Father
Dickinson (detective with kids) says don't duck boy. Father sits Joshua down; tours hardware stores; police court; judge (blond, big blue eyes, "Tk-tk-tk") commits Joshua to House of Refuge until 21 ("incorrigible"). Dickinson ridicules Cole; advice: "Don't fight back."

## Ch VIII – Number 5635
House of Refuge; superintendent (Peter D. Florence founded it — grandfather). Joshua is Number 5635. Beaver Clegg (ugly, Lincoln-like, astronomer, variable star observer, three-inch refractor) takes him as Juvenile Department ward; explains moon, variable stars, Algol.

## Ch IX – Truth and Honor
Sewing machine work; storytelling; Clegg takes Joshua to roof at night; moon through telescope (Clavius, Tycho, Blancanus, Mt. McKinley). Joshua nicknamed "Tony"; T-and-H medal (Truth and Honor). Harassed; spat on by Number 2344 (Felix Wolfgang, Norwegian).

## Ch X – Pardoned
Joshua fights 2344 deliberately to lose parole; beaten by bamboo rod. Second medal; board offers parole, he stays. Clegg dies of heart failure; will leaves telescope/books/photos to Joshua. Uncle Peter Henry Florence visits, then leaves. Joshua, 20, pardoned; takes telescope; leaves for West; Lester in shoe store refused help; Joshua boards freight; 2344 (Wolfgang) on same train.

## Ch XI – An Offer of Partnership
Pittsburgh; brakeman. Joshua tries to lecture on moon in village (Apennines, Sea of Serenity); earns $2.00 in dimes/nickels. Meets John Yegg "The Whimperer" (scarred, twisted face, artificial scar, stub-boned contortionist, peddles skeleton dance); offers partnership ("jocker"). "Youse" dialect.

## Ch XII – Whimpermeter
Whimperer's "whimpermeter" sob poem; lumps/set-downs; partnership accepted. Wolfgang meets Whimperer at night; Wolfgang gives $5; hires Whimp to watch Joshua. Joshua rides trains.

## Ch XIII – The Partnership Dissolved
Wolfgang's plan (Whimp reveals later). Whimperer learns telescope worth $500; steals it while Joshua sleeps; peddles for $100. Joshua wanders about a year in Trampdom. Joshua loses him in Colorado.

## Ch XIV – Man and the Slug
Philosophical reflection on man as human chameleon; starvation in S. Colorado; slug on stick; prayer; Joshua resolves to keep traveling West; seeks telescope and Madge.

## Ch XV – Out West
Gold Belt Cut-off railroad in California; Spur (desert town); Demarest, Spruce and Tillou contractors; stable boss; California Bill Fox (53, freighter, squat, slate-gray eyes, black brows, "character"; ex-deputy sheriff, Chaparral County). Bill says Bloodmop Mundy dead; Madge boss ("Shanty Madge").

## Ch XVI – The Road to G-String
Trip by wagon; Bill calls him "Tony"; "hi-yu skookum"; Bill mentions Jack Montgomery (son of Montgomery & Applegate). Wild Woman Springs, Box-R Ranch, Stirrup Lake, Saddle Mountain, Spyglass Mountain.

## Ch XVII – Ambitions
Joshua works hammerman at Camp One; Madge rides up (black gelding), greets him. Buys clothes ($17.35). Visits Mundys; Mrs. Mundy; tunnel through Hill of Springs; Joshua's ambitions: astronomy, a telescope, mountain observatory; Madge: "Is there any money in it?"

## Ch XVIII – New Prospects
Madge explains tunnel problems; Jawbone Mahoney powderman. Joshua confesses he came hunting her. Bill proposes homestead filing on Spyglass Mountain (forest reserve). Bill loans $40.

## Ch XIX – A Trio of Shocks
Golden (mining engineer, G-string) helps survey; Joshua files at Los Angeles land office; buys brass tubing, lens. Return to Ragtown: finds The Whimperer doing skeleton dance; chases him into tent of Felix Wolfgang (now stud dealer at The Golden Eagle, Ragtown). Learns Jawbone shot caused tunnel slide.

## Ch XX – "A Little Sleep"
Mrs. Mundy plans to file claim secretly (Joshua advises); "I'll shrive you." Joshua stops the slide: tunnel timbers, Demarest offers $2,500 (later $5,000). Joshua shot by unknown rifleman on trail, lies down: "All he wanted was a little sleep."

## Ch XXI – The Surrender
Ragtown hospital; Dr. J. Miles Stanhope (drunk, Van Dyke beard, roulette, Gladys). Madge visits; Mundys surrender outfit to Demarest, Spruce and Tillou; homestead allowed.

## Ch XXII – Hercules and His Firebrand
Joshua's plan: coyote hole around slide ("behind the pressure"); diagram A–I; Demarest (Philip, "Heavens to Betsy!") agrees; slide stopped. Joshua refuses job, plans 8-inch telescope for Mars opposition June 18 next year.

## Ch XXIII – "When the Moment Comes!"
Joshua's Mars canal theory (geometric figure communication); Jack Montgomery enters.

## Ch XXIV – Water at Ragtown
Jack Montgomery (college-educated, insincere). Joshua buys eight-inch telescope ($2,000), gray horse Argo ($500, Prince renamed), saddle. Moves Mundys. Lee Sweet (Box-R Ranch owner, giant, half-moon whiskers, drunk) threatens homesteaders; Joshua shoves him down; Bill calms him.

## Ch XXV – On the Rocky Road to Ragtown
Campfire at Spyglass; Madge and Joshua; Joshua declares love; Madge: wants money, Jack Montgomery proposing; O'Reilly poem "A Dreamer Lives Forever."

## Ch XXVI – The Moron
Bill brings Whimperer drunk on wagon. Whimperer confesses: stole telescope, sold for $100; Slim Wolfgang hired him to shadow Joshua for $25,000 deal (inheritance trap: Peter Henry Florence's $150,000 legacy to Tony at 21; if Tony absent by age 21, goes to Lester). Wolfgang shot Joshua with a .30-30. Joshua gives Whimp $10 and flask; Whimp warns Lee Sweet.

## Ch XXVII – "Nuttin' but de Trut'"
Whimp confesses full story; Joshua pays $10, Whimp takes stage to Spur.

## Ch XXVIII – "You'll Come Back to Spyglass Mountain"
Winnie the Weeper (Slim's girl) reads Whimperer's letter (signed; requests $25 via Mother Duffy, Oakland bar, Sacramento). Trail completed; Madge and Joshua at summit ("You'll come back to Spyglass Mountain").

## Ch XXIX – Winter in the San Antones
Observatory installed January; articles in The Universe, American Astronomer, Journal of Astronomy ("Is Mars a Lifeless Planet?"); The Scientist opposes; Milton University reports Eratosthenes vegetation.

## Ch XXX – Slim Wolfgang Plans
Slim tells Winnie full plot: Ole Man Cole, Lester, inheritance, Lee Sweet to be used to drive Tony out.

## Ch XXXI – Bullets from Spyglass Mountain
Madge leaves for LA with Mrs. Mundy (Montgomery invite); letter about marrying Jack. Lee Sweet fires at Joshua's cabin from shelf; Joshua calm, "Fiddlesticks."

## Ch XXXII – The Night of June Fifteenth
Sweet fires cabin, Argo stampeded. Madge's letter (June 14) breaks engagement. Bill gets Winnie & Slim to confess, binds them (June 15, Lester's 21st birthday).

## Ch XXXIII – Horsemen in the Night
Joshua on observatory June 15 night; Slim brings Joshua the confession; Bill: Lee Sweet's men shoot from horseback.

## Ch XXXIV – When the Moment Came
Joshua's signal at 12:10 on June 18 (actually recorded for Milton University, Dr. Hiram A. Buck); shots break through dome; Joshua shot. Madge returns; telegraph congratulations; Dr. Emanuel Schlott confirms photograph; Joshua recovers; "I've come back to Spyglass Mountain."

END OF BOOK 1.

# BOOK 2 — The World Masters (George Griffith, 1903)

## Prologue – The Moment of Triumph
Strassburg, night; Doctor Emil Fargeau (≈60, Alsatian scientist, lost province) breaks steel plate with mallet, invention of magnetic world-power; speech to France ("Empire of the World"). Ten 20-mark gold pieces; Weinthal (Jew money-lender) draft.

## Ch I
Jan 27 (Kaiser's birthday), German Embassy, St Petersburg. Prince Xavier de Condé (Louis Xavier), Duc de Montpensier; daughter Adelaide de Condé, Marquise de Montpensier (~21). Captain Victor Fargeau (German Uhlan, military attaché, son of Emil). Count Leo Valdemar, daughter Countess Sophie Valdemar (19, golden-bronze hair, pansy-blue eyes, skilled intriguer). Victor tells Adelaide "he has succeeded" and "goes to Paris."

## Ch II
Fargeau meets French War Minister (General Ducros) in Paris; refused (wants a thousand francs/conviction); Fargeau destroys accumulator, sells, takes Weinthal debt; ends life by jumping overboard in English Channel from steamer, tin box with specifications lashed to body.

## Ch III
May; steam yacht *Nadine*, owned by Ernest Shafto Hardress, Viscount Branston (heir of Earl of Orrel); guest Frank Lamson, D.Sc. (Cambridge). They pick up mangled body; find tin box. Lady Olive (Hardress's sister); Miss Chrysie Vandel (American, daughter of Clifford K. Vandel of Buffalo electrical storage trust).

## Ch IV
Lamson reads papers; tempted to keep for himself; then shows Hardress. Discovery: magnetic-tide control, power to draw "soul" of earth from metals.

## Ch V
Orrel Court dinner; Clifford Vandel, "Lightning King"; Lamson's exposition; syndicate formed.

## Ch VI
Hardress leases Boothia Felix (magnetic pole) from Canada; Chrysie accepts conditional engagement ("option on territory... reserve").

## Ch VII
Elsenau spa (Hôtel Wilhelmshof); Lord Orrel meets Prince de Condé; Prince tells his story; Prince's heart attack/death after learning end of story.

## Ch VIII
Prince's dying night; Adelaide nurses; madness; death (blood vessel on brain); physician certifies.

## Ch IX
Adelaide's diary (locked book) expressing love/ambition toward Victor and Hardress.

## Ch X
Hardress tells Orrel he loves Chrysie; Victor in Vienna proposes plan to Adelaide: wants French Arctic expedition.

## Ch XI–XII
Victor in Paris with Adelaide; meets General Ducros; Sophie and Count Valdemar learn plan (trapper/voyageur cable); Ducros agrees to Polar expedition plan.

## Ch XIII–XIV
Chrysie overhears; Sophie seduces engineer Edward Williams (disappointed inventor) to sabotage *Nadine* engines. Sophie plans capture of *Nadine* by Russian yacht *Vlodoya*.

## Ch XV–XVI
Storage Works built at Port Adelaide (Boothia). Lamson, Austin Vandel (nephew). Telegram: Russian and French expeditions set sail. Adelaide's letter from Victor. Chrysie reads telegram from Felice (Adelaide's maid) to Count Valdemar at Cherbourg.

## Ch XVII
Adelaide refuses Sophie's offer to betray the Trust, then agrees; Sophie's promise to spare Hardress's family.

## Ch XVIII–XIX
Nadine sails from Southampton a day early; Williams plants sabotage; Vlodoya overhauls. Punch "à le Grand Monarque" drugs crew. Chrysie stays awake with gun.

## Ch XX–XXII
Mounted guns (Vandelite 12-pounder); Williams caught sanding shaft; Vlodoya fires; Chrysie shoots from Maxim; Vlodoya surrenders; Count and Sophie taken prisoner; Vlodoya sunk.

## Ch XXIII–XXIV
Journal reports; Germany/France crisis; Trust circular (capitation fee; electrical force cutoff).

## Ch XXV–XXVI
Engines start (Chrysie pulls lever at 6). Electrical force drawn from Europe; ships break down; Charles Martel disabled; Kaiser and President Loubet meet King Edward in London; arbitration.

## Ch XXVII
Polar expeditions (Russian ice-breaker *Ivan the Terrible*; French *Caiman*, *Corneille*) arrive at Port Adelaide.

## Ch XXVIII–XXIX
Dinner at Works; Admiral Nazanoff (Russian), Admiral Dumont (French), Victor Fargeau; ultimatum. Adelaide shoots Chrysie (arm), Hardress (thigh), Lord Orrel (ear), Hardress wounded. Lamson's death-ray disintegrates Adelaide, Sophie, Victor.

## Ch XXX–XXXI
Admirals; Count Valdemar killed by death-ray at gun. Ships destroyed by Vandelite shells.

## Epilogue
Hardress and Chrysie married; Powers accept arbitration; "We are kings and queens from pole to pole."

END OF BOOK 2.

# BOOK 3 — The Chevalier's Daughter, or An Exile for the Truth (Lucy Ellen Guernsey)

## Note
Memoir of Agnes Genevieve Corbet née d'Antin (written in old age), transcribed by granddaughter Rosamond Genevieve Corbet, Tre Madoc Court, 1740. Set 1660s–1680s.

## Ch I – Early Recollections
Born 1660 at Tour d'Antin, near Sartilly, Normandy. Father Chevalier d'Antin (Provençal De Fayrolles family, Protestant). Mother Margaret Corbet (English, Cornish/Devon, pale, grey eyes). Tenants Protestant; Temple chapel. Foster-parents Simon and Jeanne Sablot; children David and Lucille. Curé Father Francois. Mount St Michael; Grève quicksands. Persecution history; Provençal Vaudois. Uncle (head of family) converted. David goes to see procession; Joshua... (no—David) goes; Vevette warns.

## Ch II – The Tour d'Antin
Returns home at age ~5/6; room in turret; Mrs. Grace (English servant). Farewell feast; curé's visit ("loup-garou" tales); Father's cousin Andrew Corbet betrothed (family arrangement).

## Ch III – Youthful Days
Reading forbidden plays (stolen book, lie, confession). Sanctity; learns English, Italian. Dream of Lord Percy. Hospital at Sartilly opened (nuns); fire and flood.

## Ch IV – Trust and Distrust
Lucille's jealousy, bitterness; Lucille apostasy (gold crucifix); Lucille's cruel farewell note; Father's secret: pastor Monsieur Bertheau to be hidden in tower; Vevette dedicated to God.

## Ch V – Guests at the Tour
Night in old grange and ruined chapel; Protestant Communion; Andrew (Cousin) arrives; vault; pastor Bertheau escapes to Jersey.

## Ch VI – The Lonely Grange
Andrew arrives (sea captain); communion in vault; Gran'mère Luchon and grandchildren taken to nuns; Pierre Le Febre.

## Ch VII – A Sudden Summons
Procession of St Michael; Lucille (now nun) seen; Mrs. Grace dies (heart); buried in vault.

## Ch VIII – Flight
Secret passage; Father killed by mob (Michaud shot him); Andrew and Vevette escape to Jersey via Pierre's boat; white cat Blanchon.

## Ch IX – In Jersey
Cousin George Corbet (rector) and Cousin Marianne; Eleanor; Vevette illness; Blanchon.

## Ch X – To England
Mother's health declines; London; Uncle Charles and Aunt Jem (Jemima); visit to Mr. Pepys; jewels sold; Simon & Jeanne; move to Cornwall.

## Ch XI – Tre Madoc
Journey to Tre Madoc; Aunt Amy (Andrew's mother); cousins Betty, Margaret (Meg), Rosamond; Deborah (housekeeper); Cornish manners.

## Ch XII – Mischief
Betty's mischief; Deborah/Jeanne quarrel; the Well House; Dinah (foundling); Vevette's jealousy; the school.

## Ch XIII – The Book
Betty's stolen book of plays; Aunt Amy's accusation; Rosamond's kindness; Vevette's ill feeling; Betty meets Lovel at Torden's cottage.

## Ch XIV – A Wedding
Vevette and Andrew split; Betty marries Lovel; Lord Stanton; Mr. Penrose; Vevette leaves Tre Madoc.

## Ch XV – Stanton Court
Mother dies at Stanton Court; Vevette's worldliness; Theo marries Dean; Lewis Stanton; Vevette leaves for London.

## Ch XVI – London
Uncle Charles (gaming), Aunt Jem (rouge, fine clothes); Mr. Goodgroome (music); Mr. Pepys; French ambassador; Marquis de Fayrolles (uncle, Catholic).

## Ch XVII – My New Friends
Marquise, Father Martien; Andrew's supposed marriage (Jamaica planter's daughter); Aunt Jem dies.

## Ch XVIII – A Great Step
Mercer refuses to accompany; Vevette converted to Catholicism; retreat; illness; Louis XIV.

## Ch XIX – Another Change
Paris; uncle's disgrace (Madame de Valliere/Montespan); Monsieur de Luynes proposes; Vevette refuses; locked in attic with gray cat.

## Ch XX – "You Shall Have No Choice"
Carriage to Marseilles; uncle strikes Huguenot preacher Morin; David Sablot seen; Ursuline convent; sees Lucille letter; Mother Mary of the Incarnation.

## Ch XXI – The Convent
Mother Mary; Desirée; Sister St Stanislaus; Lucille's death revealed (drowned); Vevette mocks Mother Mary.

## Ch XXII – The Voyage
Ship to Canada; storm; wreck; Good Hope rescues; Andrew (Captain Mayhew's guest) saves her; marriage by Mr. Norton; Boston.

## Ch XXIII – Conclusion
Lucille found (interpreter); Vevette and Andrew live at Hampton, New England; Father Martien attacks; return to Cornwall; family fates; closing moral (St James 1:8; 1 John 2:15; Matthew 6:24).

Signed: Agnes Genevieve Corbet née d'Antin. END OF BOOK 3.
